subject: Subsetting rows by passing an argument to a function

messages.author: 6d516dae6aab4320
messages.subject: Subsetting rows by passing an argument to a function
parts:
Hey all,


I have the following data frame :


> head(raw_data)
  subject block trial_num soa target_identity prime_type target_type congruency prime_exposure target_exposure button_pressed   rt ac
1      99     1         1 200              82          9           1          9              0              36              1 1253  1
2      99     1         2 102              95          2           1          2             75              36              1 1895  1
3      99     1         3  68             257          2           2          1             75              36              2 1049  1
4      99     1         4  68              62          9           1          9              0              36              1 1732  1
5      99     1         5  34             482          9           3          9              0              36              3  765  1
6      99     1         6  68              63          9           1          9              0              36              1 2027  1

I read raw_data into R using read_data() which I call inside early_prep() I created (I copied only the relevant part of the function):

early_prep <- function(file_name, keep_rows = NULL, id = NULL){

  if (is.null(id)) {
    # Stops running the function
    stop("~~~~~~~~~~~ id is missing. Please provide name of id column ~~~~~~~~~~~")
  }

  # Call read_data() function
  raw_data <- read_data(file_name)

  if (!is.null(keep_rows)) {
    raw_data <- raw_data[keep_rows, ]
    # Print to console
    print("#### Deleting unnecesarry rows in raw_data ####", quote = FALSE)

  }

  print(dim(raw_data))
  print(head(raw_data))
  return(raw_data)
  }

}

My problem is with raw_data <- raw_data[keep_rows, ]. When I enter keep_rows = "raw_data$block > 1" this is what I get:

> x1 <- early_prep(file_name = "n44.txt", keep_rows = "raw_data$block > 1", id = "subject")
[1] #### Reading txt file ####
[1] #### Deleting unnecesarry rows in raw_data ####
[1]  1 13
   subject block trial_num soa target_identity prime_type target_type congruency prime_exposure target_exposure button_pressed rt ac
NA      NA    NA        NA  NA              NA         NA          NA         NA             NA              NA             NA NA NA


How can I solve this so it will only delete the rows I want? 

I also published this question in stackoverflow 

http://stackoverflow.com/questions/30978642/subsetting-rows-by-passing-an-argument-to-a-function

Any help will be greatly appreciated

Best,

Ayala

messages.author: 9d7c257e609d0807
messages.subject: Re: [Israel RUG] Subsetting rows by passing an argument to a function
parts:
The problem is that you pass the condition as a string and not as a real condition, so R can't evaluate it when you want it to.

if you still want to pass it as string you need to parse and eval it in the right place for example:

cond = eval(parse(text=keep_rows))
raw_data = raw_data[cond,]

This should work, I think

messages.author: c7a0d087ca7b2eb2
messages.subject: Re: Subsetting rows by passing an argument to a function
parts:
hi

you can use a function in dplyr called filter_ it accepts strings as arguments (as do all functions with suffix of “_“ in dplyr)

library(dplyr)
set.seed(8)
df=data.frame(x=rnorm(10),y=runif(10))
x y
-0.08459 0.2237
0.8404 0.4079
-0.4635 0.6149
-0.5508 0.215
0.736 0.6633
-0.1079 0.9775
-0.1703 0.09775
-1.088 0.6119
-3.011 0.5276
-0.5932 0.8174 
df%>%filter_("x< -3")
x y
-3.011 0.5276

yoni

​

One more quick question on the same topic:

If I do what you suggested on the columns of my data frame (rather than on the rows), it works if I enter in the keep_col function argument a vector with the number of columns which I want to keep, but it doesn't work if I enter names of columns:
        keep_col <- eval(parse(text = keep_col))
        raw_data <- raw_data[, keep_col]

This works as an argument of the function
keep_col = "-c(2, 5)"

inside the function:
        keep_col <- eval(parse(text = keep_col))
        raw_data <- raw_data[, keep_col]

This doesn't work as an argument of the function
keep_col = "-c("block", "target_type")"

I get an error saying:
Error: unexpected symbol in "x1 <- early_prep(file_name = "n44.txt", results_name = "results_n44", id = "subject", within_vars = c("soa", "congruency"), reaction_time = "rt", accuracy = "ac", keep_col = "-c("block"

I can live with entering only number of columns instead of having the option to enter either number of columns or names, but if there is a simple way to make names of columns work also that would be great.

Thanks,

Ayala

the index comment amit gave is regarding the low level functions of data frames and not dplyr.

raw_data%>%select(-one_of("a","b"))


a note on using dplyr:

putting the dataframe in the command like select/filter/mutate is redundant. it is implied in the command that select is applied on the object to the left of %>%. this makes the chains easier to understand and run parts of them

for example:

lets say df has 4 columns a,b,c,d and a is numeric and d is either a character or factor.

the code below is like a sentence:

take df select a and d filter all rows where a<10 and calculate the sum of a by the levels of d into a new variable named e

df%>%select(a,d)%>%filter(a<10)%>%group_by(d)%>%summarise(e=sum(a))

it also allows you to run pieces of the chain if needed which comes in handy.

On Tue, Jun 23, 2015 at 1:42 PM, Yoni Sidi <yon...@gmail.com> wrote:

the index comment amit gave is regarding the low level functions of data frames and not dplyr.

raw_data%>%select(-one_of("a","b"))


a note on using dplyr:

putting the dataframe in the command like select/filter/mutate is redundant. it is implied in the command that select is applied on the object to the left of %>%. this makes the chains easier to understand and run parts of them

for example:

lets say df has 4 columns a,b,c,d and a is numeric and d is either a character or factor.

the code below is like a sentence:

take df select a and d filter all rows where a<10 and calculate the sum of a by the levels of d into a new variable named e

df%>%select(a,d)%>%filter(a<10)%>%group_by(d)%>%summarise(e=sum(a))

it also allows you to run pieces of the chain if needed which comes in handy.

The problem is that you pass the condition as a string and not as a real condition, so R can't evaluate it when you want it to.

if you still want to pass it as string you need to parse and eval it in the right place for example:

cond = eval(parse(text=keep_rows))
raw_data = raw_data[cond,]

This should work, I think
